title: PD 957 License to Sell Registration Gate
subject: Planning / Housing / Building Laws

questions.stem: A subdivision project has been registered, but no license to sell has been issued. Under the cited PD 957 IRR excerpt, may the owner/dealer sell disposable lots or units?

options.B: Yes, if brochures have been submitted.
options.C: No, the license to sell is still required.
options.D: Yes, if the project has a billboard notice.

rationale.correct: Section 11 says no owner or dealer shall sell without a license to sell issued by the Board.

distractors.A: Registration and selling authority are separate in the cited excerpt.
distractors.B: Public-offering materials are part of application evidence, not the license itself.
distractors.D: Posting/publication evidence does not replace the license to sell.

rationale.takeaway: When the stem asks selling authority, look for the license to sell.

questions.source_locator: PD 957 IRR, Rule IV, Section 11, PDF p.47.

questions.stem: The cited Section 11 ties issuance of the license to sell to which project event?

options.A: Within two weeks from registration of each project
options.B: Within two weeks from final occupancy inspection
options.C: Only after all units are fully paid
options.D: Only after turnover of the condominium corporation

rationale.correct: The extracted Section 11 text says within two weeks from the registration of each project.

distractors.B: Occupancy inspection is not the event stated in the cited Section 11 text.
distractors.C: Full payment by buyers is unrelated to license issuance in this excerpt.
distractors.D: Condominium corporation turnover is not the cited timing trigger.

rationale.takeaway: Tie the timing to registration, then check the other application requirements.

questions.source_locator: PD 957 IRR, Rule IV, Section 11, PDF p.47.

questions.stem: Which document type is explicitly included among public-offering materials in the cited PD 957 application evidence?

rationale.correct: The excerpt lists circular, prospectus, brochure, advertisement, or communication for public offering.

distractors.B: A plumbing fixture schedule is not named in the cited public-offering list.
distractors.C: A fire drill certificate is not named in the cited public-offering list.
distractors.D: The cited list is broader and specifically names offering materials.

rationale.takeaway: Do not confuse sales/public-offering evidence with unrelated technical submittals.

questions.source_locator: PD 957 IRR, application documentary requirement excerpt, PDF p.43.
